Here’s a simple, inexpensive-ish prep lineup:

### 1) Lemon-garlic lentil salad
[Budget Bytes recipe](https://www.budgetbytes.com/lentil-salad/)

- **Makes:** 6 servings; about **30 minutes** total. The source estimates **$1.22 per serving**.
- **Main ingredients:** brown lentils, lemon, olive oil, garlic, oregano, parsley, tomatoes, red onion, feta.
- **Key cooking info:** Boil 1 cup brown lentils in 3 cups water for about **20 minutes**; drain and cool. Toss with the lemon-garlic dressing and vegetables.
- **Meal-prep note:** Keeps **3–4 days** in the fridge and is eaten cold. Use brown/green lentils—not red/orange, which get too soft. Add chickpeas, cucumber, rice, or rotisserie chicken if you want it more substantial.

### 2) Veggie-loaded turkey chili
[Bowl of Delicious recipe](https://www.bowlofdelicious.com/crockpot-turkey-and-vegetable-chili/)

- **Makes:** 6 servings; **15-minute prep** and at least **30 minutes** stovetop cooking.
- **Main ingredients:** 1 lb ground turkey, onion, bell pepper, zucchini, corn, black beans, crushed tomatoes, broth, garlic, and chili spices. A little cocoa powder is optional but adds depth.
- **Key cooking info:** Sauté onion and pepper 3–5 minutes; add garlic/spices; brown turkey with zucchini; then add everything else and simmer, covered, **30 minutes** (or longer for fuller flavor).
- **Make-ahead options:** Slow cooker: **3–4 hours on high** or **7–8 hours on low**. Instant Pot: **20 minutes on high**, then **10-minute natural release**.
- **Storage:** Freeze portions in airtight containers for up to **6 months**. Cheap, filling, and a good way to stretch one pound of turkey.

### 3) Chocolate peanut-butter energy bites
[A Couple Cooks recipe](https://www.acouplecooks.com/energy-bites/)

- **Makes:** 20 bites; **15 minutes**, no baking.
- **Main ingredients:** rolled oats, cocoa, a small amount of mini chocolate chips, coconut, peanut butter, honey, cinnamon, and salt.
- **Key cooking info:** Mix, starting with slightly less oats; freeze the mixture **5 minutes**, then roll. If crumbly, add a little peanut butter/honey; if sticky, add oats.
- **Storage:** Refrigerate up to **2 weeks**. Sunflower butter or tahini can replace peanut butter; agave can replace honey.

### 4) Carrot-cake energy bites
[EatingWell recipe](https://www.eatingwell.com/recipe/273188/carrot-cake-energy-bites/)

- **Makes:** 22 bites; **15 minutes**, no cooking.
- **Main ingredients:** dates, oats, pecans, chia seeds, carrots, vanilla, cinnamon, ginger, turmeric.
- **Key cooking info:** Pulse dates, oats, pecans, and chia; add carrot and spices; process into a paste and roll into scant tablespoon-size balls.
- **Storage:** Airtight in the fridge for **up to 1 week**, or freeze for **up to 3 months**.

**Easy plan:** Make chili and lentil salad for lunches/dinners, then pick one energy-bite recipe for a sweet grab-and-go option—or make both and freeze half.
